description: §4.12.3 — a nested `<program name= lang= mode="wasm">` is a WASM COMPUTE MODULE, whose runtime model is `WebAssembly.instantiate()`. That codegen is Nominal/spec-ahead, so the declaration fails closed with E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL and the compiler emits NEITHER a `new Worker(...)` reference NOR a bundle. Pre-fix (S356) the extraction pre-pass claimed EVERY `name=`d nested `<program>` as a §4.12.4 inline web worker, so this shape compiled exit-0 to `new Worker("<base>.calc.worker.js")` plus a 25-byte bundle containing one comment line — a file that returns 200, LOADS, and never assigns `self.onmessage`, turning `<#calc>.send()` into a Promise that never resolves. A silent hang is worse than the 404 it replaced.
rationale: §4.12.3's table gives "WASM compute module | `name=`, `lang=`, `mode=\"wasm\"` | `WebAssembly.instantiate()`" as a type distinct from the inline web worker. §4.12.3 normative (S356): "a nested `<program>` SHALL be compiled as a §4.12.4 inline web worker … if and only if it carries `name=` and carries none of `lang=`, `mode=`, `route=`, `db=`, `port=`", and "Where an execution context's codegen is not implemented in a given compiler revision, that revision SHALL emit NEITHER a reference to the context … NOR an artifact standing in for it, and SHALL fail closed with a diagnostic naming the context."
